subject: Energy
title: The Lithium Supply Chain
description: Learn The Lithium Supply Chain in one minute.

hook.text: Lithium comes from brine pools in Chile and Argentina or hard-rock mines in Australia—supply is concentrated.

buildup.text: Brine extraction evaporates saltwater over months—hard-rock mining crushes spodumene ore to extract lithium carbonate.

discovery.text: Demand is surging—EVs and grid storage could require 5–10x more lithium by 2030 than is mined today.

twist.text: There's no geological shortage—lithium is abundant in Earth's crust, but building new mines takes 5–10 years.

climax.text: Recycling, sodium-ion alternatives, and direct lithium extraction from geothermal brines could ease supply pressure.

punchline.text: Abundant in the crust, slow to mine—lithium's bottleneck is time.

quiz.question: Is there a geological shortage of lithium?
options: No, but building new mines takes years
